objective.statement: Add a small calendar widget to HomeView.tsx that lets the user select a date, and display the selected date in the UI.

acceptanceCriteria.statement: HomeView renders a small calendar widget that shows a month grid of days.
The user can select a date by activating a day in the grid, and the selected day is visibly marked.
The selected date is displayed as text in the UI; before any selection the UI shows 'No date selected'.
The user can move to the previous and next month so dates outside the initial month can be selected.

The widget is operable by keyboard and by assistive technology: day cells are buttons with a full-date accessible name and aria-pressed for the selected day, and the selected-date text is announced politely when it changes.
The existing HomeView sections and their tests are unchanged.

in.statement: Add a CalendarWidget component with test ids and component tests, a small pure month-grid helper in src/lib with unit tests, and render the widget in HomeView.tsx with a HomeView component test.

out.statement: New dependencies (no date or calendar library), persisting the selection (store, URL or storage), events or scheduling, date ranges, min/max limits, internationalisation beyond a fixed en-US format, changes to other HomeView sections, and historical workflow records.

observations.statement: The calendar is hand-built from native Date and Intl, so no dependency is needed. It is a month grid with weekday headers, weeks starting on Sunday, and leading and trailing blank cells.
Initial state: no date is selected, the shown month is the current month, and the text reads 'No date selected'. Preselecting today was rejected as the more surprising behaviour.

Selected-date text uses a fixed en-US long format, for example 'Wednesday, November 25, 2026', built from local-time Date values (never parsed from ISO strings) so the day cannot shift with the time zone. Selecting the selected day again keeps it selected.

Placement: a separate full-width section after the existing torus row in HomeView, because the 200px torus row holds fixed-size widgets and a month grid is wider. The card says only 'on the HomeView.tsx'.

State is local to CalendarWidget (selected date and visible month); nothing is shared, stored or fetched. Styling follows Clock.tsx: Tailwind classes, the surface and border tokens, and data-id test ids from a CalendarWidget.testIds.ts file.
